question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r={csc}^{3}⁡\theta \,$ for $\pi /3\le \theta \le \pi /2?$
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={csc}^{3}⁡\theta \,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-3{csc}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the expression for our line integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{({csc}^{3}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(-3{csc}^{3}⁡\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{csc}^{6}⁡\theta +9{csc}^{6}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{csc}^{6}⁡\theta (1+9{cot}^{2}⁡\theta })\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}{csc}^{3}⁡\theta \sqrt{1+9{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
